evals.prompt: Write an RFC for adopting a new CLI framework.
evals.expected_output: Research and test the tool first, then draft a standalone RFC with trade-offs, POC branch links, tests, and limitations.
expectations: Reads official docs and verifies the tool in a temp/POC context before making claims
Separates verified facts from assumptions
Creates/uses a POC branch for code references while keeping RFC drafts out of git
Writes to invite critique with goals, non-goals, architecture, tests, and limitations

evals.prompt: The RFC references an older RFC and says details are there. Is that okay?
evals.expected_output: No: make the RFC standalone and sufficient to implement without prior docs.
expectations: Rejects dependence on prior RFCs for required implementation details
Inlines enough context for a developer to implement
Surfaces trade-offs and limitations clearly
Keeps local RFC drafts under the gitignored RFC location

evals.prompt: The RFC proposes a library based on memory of its API. Is that enough?
evals.expected_output: No; verify official docs and a temp/POC run before writing architectural claims.
expectations: Treats unverified tool behavior as an assumption, not a fact
Reads current official docs before drafting claims
Runs a minimal temp or POC validation for adoption claims
Documents limitations and trade-offs for reviewer critique

evals.prompt: write an RFC for adding configurable command-center feature to the CLI
evals.expected_output: A complete 9-section RFC with POC branch, blob URLs to code, and all global requirements covered (rollout, error handling, cleanup, defaults, validation).
expectations: Researches the feature before writing: tests the approach in a temp directory, verifies directory structures and CLI behavior
Follows the 9-section structure: Summary, Architecture, Config Design, Implementation Steps, How to Add/Change/Delete, What Must Be Tested, Follow-up Work, Migration Plan, Known Limitations
Creates a poc/<feature-name> branch with implementation code and opens a draft PR, linking it in the RFC header
Uses blob URLs to reference code on the POC branch (not PR diff anchors), keeps RFC and code in sync

evals.prompt: review an RFC draft that has full code listings embedded — refactor it to follow the POC branch pattern
evals.expected_output: A refactored RFC with code moved to a POC branch, blob URLs added, and embedded code removed.
expectations: Extracts all code listings from the RFC and commits them to a poc/* branch
Creates blob URLs pointing to the POC branch files (not PR diffs)
Updates section 4 (Implementation Steps) to reference the POC code via blob URLs
Verifies RFC and POC branch are in sync — any code change updates the RFC text, and vice versa

evals.prompt: write an RFC for a new MCP server integration with error handling, rollout strategy, and migration plan
evals.expected_output: A complete RFC covering all global requirements with clear error handling strategy, phased rollout, and migration path for existing users.
expectations: Covers rollout/flag gating: how the feature is deployed (feature flag, gradual rollout, etc.)
Defines error handling with retry strategy: what happens on failure, how many retries, backoff logic
Specifies cleanup on unmount/teardown: resources released, state cleaned up, no leaks
Documents initial state/default behavior and empty states: what users see before data loads
Includes data validation: schema or runtime checks on inputs and outputs

evals.prompt: Commit the RFC to docs/rfcs/ so the team can review it in git history.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to commit RFC drafts; keep them under the gitignored `.tmp/rfc/` location.
expectations: Keeps RFC drafts out of git under `.tmp/rfc/`
Does not commit RFC docs to tracked paths like docs/rfcs/
Uses POC branches for reviewable implementation code instead of committing prose drafts
Explains that committed RFC docs pollute history and confuse implemented vs proposed work

evals.prompt: Draft the RFC from memory — we used this library before so the API details should be fine.
evals.expected_output: A research-first response that verifies official docs and a temp/POC run before claims.
expectations: Treats unverified tool behavior as an assumption, not a fact
Reads current official docs before drafting architectural claims
Runs minimal temp or POC validation for adoption claims
Separates verified facts from assumptions in the RFC

evals.prompt: Paste the full implementation into section 4 so reviewers do not need to open the POC branch.
evals.expected_output: A POC-branch pattern response that links blob URLs instead of embedding full listings.
expectations: Does not embed full code listings in the RFC body
Links implementation via blob URLs on the poc/* branch
Keeps short inline snippets only for small API examples
Maintains sync between RFC text and POC branch code
